newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS - Arakis both ways, Chubb selling.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS - Arakis both ways, Chubb selling.

text.p: Investors were playing both sides of Arakis Energy Corp after a big runup in the stock on Thursday and were liquidating positions in Chubb Corp as that stock rallied sharply, traders said Friday.
Arakis shares fell 11/16 to 4-25/32 after falling as low as 4-5/8. Turnover was heavy at more than 3.8 million shares.
On Thursday, shares of the Canadian energy company rallied nearly a point to close at 5-2/16, their highest close since June 21.
Traders said the stock rallied on talk the company had signed up partners for its venture in Sudan.
A Sudanese rebel leader warned Arakis Friday that his forces would strike if needed to halt any attempts to develop its concessions in southern Sudan that would benefit the Khartoum government.
Traders said the stock was more likely down on a consolidation rather than the rebel leader's threat.
"Every time they (Arakis) get in the news, that happens," one options trader said of the threat.
"I just think this is more a general pullback from a stock that was up 20 percent in one day," he said, adding that investors were playing both sides of the options.
"Basically there are players on both sides," he said. "It's a five dollar stock so the options are cheap."
"There's not one particular thing going on," he said.
Most of the activity was on the call side, led by the November five calls, which traded more than 3,000 contracts. The options traded at prices ranging from 3/8 to 11/16.
The Arakis January five call, which had the most open interest of any of the Arakis options with 14,400, traded around 2,500 contracts. It was off 3/8 at 1-1/8 in late trade.
Nearly 2,000 contracts were added to its open interest Thursday.
"A lot of people saw it trading up and jumped in, and today you're just seeing a normal pullback," the trader said.
The stock reached an intraday high of 5-5/8 Thursday.
Among Arakis puts, the January five was most active, with turnover of 555. Its open interest, including an addition of about 2,225 Thursday, was 3,800.
Chubb rallied 5-1/2 to 51 on consolidated volume of about 3.5 million shares. Traders said investors were taking profits on positions in the stock established over the last couple of weeks.
The stock fell sharply Thursday after the big insurance company reported quarterly earnings that traders said were slightly disappointing.
But a bullish conference call late Thursday drove the stock up on Friday, traders said.
"There was retail (options) buying in the last two or three weeks in anticipation of the earnings," said a trader at the New York Stock Exchange, where Chubb options trade.
"Most of today's action is just liquidation of those positions," he said. The busiest Chubb option was the November 50 call, which traded nearly 1,000 contracts.
